entities.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
entities.description: A technique that enhances large language model outputs by grounding them in relevant external documents retrieved at query time.
entities.source_sentence: # Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

relationships.description: The technique itself is the subject of the concept.

entities.name: RAG
entities.description: A technology that addresses issues related to knowledge management in large language models.
entities.source_sentence: RAG systems also support citations — since the answer is grounded in specific retrieved passages, the system can point to exact source documents, improving interpretability and trustworthiness.

entities.name: knowledge management
entities.description: The process of organizing and managing knowledge within a system.
entities.source_sentence: Large language models store knowledge implicitly in their weights during training.

entities.name: training cutoff date
entities.description: The date after which the knowledge in a large language model is considered outdated or incorrect.
entities.source_sentence: This creates several problems: the knowledge has a training cutoff date, it can be hallucinated or misremembered, and updating it requires expensive retraining.

entities.name: hallucination
entities.description: The phenomenon where a large language model generates incorrect or misleading information.
entities.source_sentence: This creates several problems: the knowledge has a training cutoff date, it can be hallucinated or misremembered, and updating it requires expensive retraining.

entities.name: misremembered
entities.description: The phenomenon where a large language model retains incorrect or outdated information.
entities.source_sentence: This creates several problems: the knowledge has a training cutoff date, it can be hallucinated or misremembered, and updating it requires expensive retraining.

entities.name: retrieved passages
entities.description: The specific pieces of information that a large language model uses to generate an answer.
entities.source_sentence: RAG systems also support citations — since the answer is grounded in specific retrieved passages, the system can point to exact source documents, improving interpretability and trustworthiness.

entities.name: interpretability
entities.description: The ability to understand and explain the reasoning behind a decision or conclusion.
entities.source_sentence: RAG systems also support citations — since the answer is grounded in specific retrieved passages, the system can point to exact source documents, improving interpretability and trustworthiness.

entities.name: trustworthiness

entities.description: The self-attention mechanism allows the model to weigh the importance of different tokens in a sequence when encoding a particular token.

entities.name: Attention Score
entities.description: The attention score between two tokens is computed as the dot product of their Query and Key vectors, scaled by the square root of the key dimension.

entities.name: Softmax
